## Lab 07 Assignment - Group 20

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)  # devtools::install_github("tidymodels/broom")
library(cowplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(factoextra)
```

```{r}
biopsy <- read_csv("https://wilkelab.org/classes/SDS348/data_sets/biopsy.csv")
```

```{r}
pca_fit <- biopsy %>% 
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>% # retain only numeric columns
  prcomp(scale = TRUE) # do PCA on scaled data

pca_fit
```

```{r}
pca_fit <- biopsy %>% 
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>% # retain only numeric columns
  scale() %>% # scale data
  prcomp() # do PCA

pca_fit
```

## Principal Component Analysis Biplot

To visualize the relationships between the original numeric attributes and the principal components, we construct a PCA biplot using the \`factoextra\` package. This plot projects the observations onto the first two principal components (PC_1 and PC_2) while displaying the feature loading vectors to indicate how each variable contributes to the components. The samples are grouped by their true diagnostic status (\`benign\` vs. \`malignant\`) with 95% confidence ellipses to illustrate class separation.

```{r}
biopsy_clean <- biopsy |> 
  drop_na()

fviz_pca_biplot(
  pca_fit,
  geom.ind = "point",
  col.ind = biopsy_clean$outcome,
  palette = "jco",
  addEllipses = TRUE,
  ellipse.level = 0.95,
  col.var = "black",
  repel = TRUE,
  legend.title = "Outcome"
) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "PCA Plot for Biopsy Data",
       caption = "Plot Design from \nhttps://www.r-bloggers.com/2026/06/pca-in-r-principal-component-analysis-step-by-step-prcomp-ggplot2/#google_vignette",
       subtitle = "Projection of samples and feature loadings onto PC1 and PC2") +
  theme(
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, color = "gray30")
  )
```
